name: Facial Boundary Frequency
algorithm: Facial Boundary Frequency — Frequency Domain Analyzer
mechanism:
This method analyzes frequency characteristics at facial boundaries for deepfake detection:

1. **Boundary Region Extraction**: The boundary zone between the face and surrounding content (hair, neck, background) is extracted as a narrow strip. This boundary is where face-swap blending produces the most detectable frequency-domain artifacts.

2. **Local Frequency Analysis**: Spatial frequency content in the boundary strip is analyzed via localized 2D FFT or wavelet transforms. The frequency characteristics on the face side vs. the background side of the boundary are compared. Different generation/capture pipelines produce different frequency signatures.

3. **Frequency Transition Profiling**: The transition of frequency content across the boundary is measured. Natural face boundaries show smooth frequency transitions. Deepfake blending creates characteristic frequency discontinuities — typically a high-frequency step (different noise levels) or spectral notch (frequency content removed by low-pass blending).

4. **Periodic Artifact Detection**: The method specifically searches for periodic frequency artifacts at the boundary that arise from: (a) resampling/interpolation during face alignment, (b) GAN generator architecture (checkerboard patterns from transposed convolutions), (c) encoder-decoder quantization in autoencoder-based face swaps.

5. **Multi-Orientation Frequency Scanning**: The boundary frequency content is analyzed at multiple orientations. Natural boundaries show orientation-dependent frequency content (hair has directional texture, skin is more isotropic). Deepfake boundaries may show unnatural frequency isotropy or orientation-dependent artifacts from the blending direction.
parameters:
Analysis type: frequency
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through facial boundary frequency analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
